newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN NMKN'S COUMANS JOINS VAN DEN BRANDE STAFF.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN NMKN'S COUMANS JOINS VAN DEN BRANDE STAFF.

text.p: Wim Coumans, chief executive officer of Belgian industrial credit bank NMKN/SNCI, will leave the bank to become chief aide of Flemish Minister-President Luc Van den Brande.
Coumans, confirming a report in Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd, told Reuters that he himself had taken the initiative to apply for the job.
"I am going back to politics," Coumans said.
Before joining NMKN in 1991, Coumans worked in several ministerial cabinets, including that of Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
Coumans' current post will disappear as retail bank ASLK-CGER merges with NMKN this year.
ASLK, a 49.9 percent unit of Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis, acquired a 98.2 percent stake in NMKN from the Belgian state in November 1995.
A spokesman for ASLK said that the NMKN name would be kept on the branch offices of its network, but that the two banks were set for a full legal merger.
